name: HydroNet
description: Intermolecular and long-range interactions are central to phenomena as diverse as gene regulation, topological states of quantum materials, electrolyte transport in batteries, and the universal solvation properties of water. We present a set of challenge problems for preserving intermolecular interactions and structural motifs in machine-learning approaches to chemical problems, through the use of a recently published dataset of 4.95 million water clusters held together by hydrogen bonding interactions and resulting in longer range structural patterns. The dataset provides spatial coordinates as well as two types of graph representations, to accommodate a variety of machine-learning practices.
evaluation_method: MAE / RMSE (regression metrics for energy/force/property prediction); structural metrics (RMSD) for geometry/structure tasks
general_score_metric: MAE (mean absolute error) on predicted energies/forces
reputation: Moderately used within the computational chemistry / ML-for-molecules community as a challenging dataset for modelling hydrogen-bonded water clusters and long‑range interactions.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focusing on molecular modelling. Large dataset (~4.95M clusters) with both coordinate and graph representations. Challenges include long-range many-body interactions and potential simulation bias; some tasks require precise force/energy regression rather than classification.
